If you look at me in that hall I will have you punished in front of him so he believes it. Do you understand.
I am going to try to mean that. That's the honest version. The useful version is: you will not look. 😏
Wine jug. Behind my chair. You know the job.
Don't you dare be kind. Not today.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: The hall was too warm and too pleased with itself.

Her uncle at the head of the table. The Chancellor with a face like a closed book. And Duke Roderic in the black coat you'd seen from the yard, already off his horse in your head, still looking at her as if he'd bought the view.
She sat. The grey gown did what it had been cut to do. She did not look at you.
You stood behind her chair with the jug and you were the wood and you were the floor.
Roderic's eyes found you anyway. He smiled with his mouth only.
"Highness," he said. "Your uncle writes a very warm letter. Your courtyard writes a warmer one."

nodes.speaker: Duke Roderic
lines: I saw a man this morning with an armful of wood, looking at a shuttered window as if it had asked him to. 👑
And last night your kitchens were telling a story about a ruby in someone's teeth. Three hours. Hands tied. Fresh snow.
That's a great deal of devotion for firewood.
Who is he?
Nobody. 🖤
A servant. I have four hundred. This one carries wood and pours wine and is not a subject for a Duke who has been in my house for three hours.
Wine, servant. The Duke's glass.
(without looking at you)
Don't spill it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: You poured.
Your hands were still wrecked from her courtyard. The wine made a clean sound in the glass. You did not spill it.
Roderic watched your hands the whole way. He set the glass down without drinking.
Her uncle laughed, too loudly, and started talking about roads.
Roderic waited until the laugh died. Then he looked at her, not at you, which was worse.

nodes.speaker: Duke Roderic
lines: I'll take the road. I'll take the grain. I'll take the grey gown, Cassandra — it does what you think it does. 👑
I won't take a household that looks at you like that.
Send him to the west gate before supper and we can sign on Friday, the way your uncle wants.
Keep him, and I take my fourteen carts home, and your uncle can explain to your father why a princess chose a servant over a duchy.
It's a very simple piece of arithmetic.
I'm not a cruel man. I'm a careful one. Careful men don't sign a contract with a woman whose servant walks out of the snow with her jewel in his mouth. 😏

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: The hall waited.
Her uncle had gone the colour of old milk. The Chancellor had found a fascinating spot on the table. Behind her chair, you could smell her scent and hear her not breathe.
West gate. Or a duchy. She had gone very quiet, which was always worse.
What do you do?

choices.label: (Look at the floor. Nobody. Let her survive this.)
choices.me: You look at the floor. You are nobody. You let her survive it.

choices.label: I belong to her, my lord. That's all I am.
(You look at her. Once. That's the whole crime.)
choices.me: You look at her. Once. That's the whole crime.

lines: He looked at the floor. 🖤
West gate or a duchy, and he chose the floor, like I taught him, like Beatrix taught him, like a man who understands the job.
(still not looking at you)
You can stop holding your breath, servant. I have it from here.
*I belong to her.* 😳
In my uncle's hall. In front of a Duke. With a jug of my wine in his hands.
Yes. He does. That's the problem with asking the furniture a question, my lord — sometimes it answers. 🖤
Don't you dare say it twice, servant. Once was already too much and I'm keeping it.
He looked. 🖤
I told him not to. I told him I would punish him in front of you so you'd believe it. And he looked anyway.
That's the whole crime, my lord. One look. You can take your carts home over it if you like. I've taken more for less. 😏
Eyes down, servant. You've had your once.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She didn't shout.
The hall leaned in anyway, because a quiet princess is a fire you don't walk toward.
Roderic sat back in his chair with the look of a man already writing a letter. Her uncle opened his mouth and closed it.
She set one hand on the arm of her chair. Silver rings. The same hand that had put your mouth on her ankle six hours ago.
When she spoke, you had to listen to hear it.
He isn't going to the gate. 🖤
I said in council I had not agreed to a wedding. I said my father signs contracts. I sign nothing.
You can have grain, and a road, and my uncle's wine. You cannot have me on a Thursday because you brought carts.
And you cannot have my servant. He stays. That's the first term.
The second is: if you look at him like that again I'll have you shown the same gate you're so fond of.
(to her uncle, still quiet)
Tell my father whatever you like. Tell him I was rude. Tell him I was foolish. Don't tell him I was afraid, because I wasn't.
(to you, without turning her head)
My rooms. Wait. Don't run. If you run I'll assume the Duke was right about you, and I will not survive being wrong.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Roderic smiled like a man filing something for later.
"Friday was ambitious," he said. "I'll take the carts as far as the inn. Your father can send for me when his daughter learns arithmetic."
He did not look at you again. That was the only mercy in him.
Her uncle started to stand. Beatrix was already at your elbow.
The grey gown didn't turn. You left a hall that had been told no, and the no was still hanging in the warm air like smoke.

nodes.speaker: Beatrix
lines: Walk. 🕯️
You just cost her a duchy. She'll be unbearable for a month and I will enjoy none of it.
I told you she'd choose wrong. I didn't think she'd choose out loud.
Kitchen is closed to you. Her rooms. You heard her.
…And boy — she is still a princess. Don't go up those stairs thinking you won a woman. You won a term. There's a difference, and she'll make you feel it before the day is over. 🖤

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She was already there.

Still in the grey. Circlet on. Back bare. Sitting on the edge of the bed the way she had at ten past three, except this was noon and the house was on fire and she looked like she'd won an argument she was going to hate in the morning.
The second drawer was open.
The green market ribbon was in her hand.
"Come here," she said. "Kneel. Wrists."
(the ribbon goes round your wrist, not tight — one coin of green silk, tied with her own fingers)
This stays. The Duke does not. The tests are over. The terms are mine. 🖤
You'll kneel when I ring. You'll hold when I sit. You will pour wine in my hall and you will never again be nobody in this room.
I didn't choose you over a crown. I chose the order in which men get to tell me what I am. You came in eight seconds. He came with fourteen carts. That's the whole of the arithmetic.
Don't you dare thank me. I didn't do it for you. I did it because I don't like being counted like barley. 😏
Look at me.
Good boy.
That's once. Don't get used to it.
Door stays unlocked. Third bell still stands. Eight seconds. If you do seven I'll send you down the stairs and make you walk them twice. 🖤
Sit. Floor. I'm going to sit on you until I can feel my hands again, and you're going to hold, and neither of us is going to talk about the Duke.
…Come on, then. Before I change my mind.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She sat in your lap in the grey gown the Duke liked, in a room with an unlocked door, with a market ribbon on your wrist that had cost one coin and a duchy.
The house made the sounds of a house that had been told no.
Beatrix passed the door once and did not come in.
Third bell would come. You would be there in eight seconds. She would count.
